description: Platform support-routing policy used to ground the A6 customer inquiry classifier. Synthetic internal policy, no customer data.

records.title: Billing queue ownership
records.content: Billing owns duplicate or unauthorized charges, refunds, invoices, receipts, subscription cancellation, plan or price changes, payment methods, and failed payments. A charge or refund dispute belongs to billing even when the customer also mentions a delivery problem or a login problem. Refunds above USD 100 require human approval.

records.title: Technical queue ownership
records.content: Technical owns product errors, checkout or API failures, crashes, broken pages, performance problems, and outages. Technical owns the ticket when the platform failure is the primary blocker, for example checkout returning 500 for all customers. A charge mentioned only as an impact does not move the ticket to billing.

records.title: Account queue ownership
records.content: Account owns login, password reset, 2FA, verification codes, profile or email changes, data export or deletion, locked accounts, and account compromise. Choose account when access itself is the blocker or when security is involved. If login is mentioned only as a way to check an order or payment, do not choose account; route the underlying money or delivery issue instead.

records.title: Shipping queue ownership
records.content: Shipping owns delivery status, tracking, late or missing parcels, damaged items, returns, exchanges, and carrier issues. Choose shipping when the customer asks for a replacement or an exchange. If the customer explicitly disputes a charge or asks for money back, billing owns the ticket and shipping handles the physical case as a secondary task.

records.title: General triage and pre-sales
records.content: General triage (other) owns pre-sales questions, discount or eligibility questions, product availability, partnerships, press, feedback, job applications, and spam. Pre-sales pricing or discount questions are not billing unless the customer is disputing a completed charge or asking for money back.

records.title: Multi-intent routing priority
records.content: When a message contains several issues, choose exactly one queue using this priority order: (1) account security or compromise, (2) money at risk such as a duplicate or unauthorized charge or a refund, (3) physical delivery, return, or replacement, (4) technical failure, (5) information or pre-sales. A login problem that only prevents the customer from checking an order or payment is not a security issue and must not outrank the money issue. The other issues are handled as secondary tasks.

records.title: Urgency and human review policy
records.content: Urgency: critical for account compromise, legal threat or chargeback, safety issue, or a widespread outage; high for a blocked workflow, money at risk, repeated failure, or a premium or business customer; normal for a routine request; low for informational or pre-sales questions. Human review is required for security incidents, legal threats, refunds above USD 100, and any message with three or more distinct issues.
